correctness.rationale: Every non-forcing seed set is disjoint from a fort and conversely; the 128-state local fort machine is therefore exact. The finite reachable-state closure of the product with the explicit thirteen-template language checks all possible columns of arbitrary length (926 reachable product states), not a bounded experiment. A second closure (245 states) excludes all sets of size at most two. The 13-pattern intersection graph proves the component metrics, and an independently implemented direct forcing enumerator checks n=3 through n=10. Two extracted standalone scripts passed. The proof does not claim unrestricted grid widths.

value.rationale: The reconfiguration of minimum forcing sets is a natural structural refinement of the classical grid zero forcing invariant. This all-length classification identifies exactly which optimal configurations exist and explains a sharp stability transition: the exchange space of 26 configurations is connected at n=4 but splits into two fixed 13-vertex end-anchored sectors for every n>=5. Each sector's exact degrees, radius and diameter quantify local mobility. This is a motivated complete classification, not a small arbitrary parameter slice or a mere repetition of the known minimum forcing cardinality.
